blockers.evidence: aso-parent-null.json null_ensembles holds exactly ten arms: scrambled_mononucleotide, scrambled_dinucleotide, random_uniform, random_composition_matched, wings_scrambled_gap_held, gap_scrambled_wings_held, random_parent_chimera, donor_terminus_chimera, exon_terminus_chimera, exon_terminus_chimera_novel_acceptor. research/modalities/aso_parent_null.py describes them: random_uniform is "16-mers drawn i.i.d. from equal base frequencies" and random_composition_matched "16-mers drawn i.i.d. from the pooled base composition of the 190 real target windows" — neither is a scramble of any design; random_parent_chimera joins "a random window of a real donor parent to a random window of real NR4A3" — not exon termini; draw_donor_terminus_chimera's own docstring is "Chimera whose donor half ENDS AT A REAL EXON 3' TERMINUS; NR4A3 half uniform interior" — only one of the two ends is a real terminus. Only exon_terminus_chimera and exon_terminus_chimera_novel_acceptor answer the sentence's chimera description and only scrambled_mononucleotide / scrambled_dinucleotide answer its scramble description. blockers.why_a_reader_would_be_misled: Methods is where a referee or a replicator learns what null models the central 45.8%-vs-40.6% comparison was run against. As written, the paper states that all ten ensembles are scrambles of the designs or same-parent exon-terminus chimeras. Four of them are not, including the two i.i.d. random arms a reader would most expect a null to be and the arm the module calls "THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE ANCHOR". The unquantified sentence it replaced ("Null ensembles were built as scrambles … and as chimeras …") read as a partial description; adding the count makes it an enumeration, and the enumeration is wrong.

p1s.summary: Nothing reads the reference list inside the .docx that Qeios consumes. The one instrument that checks printed reference numbering against the prose reads a different artifact (the two-column journal PDF), and the .docx's own gate asserts only floors that a lost reference section would clear.
p1s.evidence: test_journal_references_match_the_prose.py::test_the_printed_pdf_numbers_the_references_as_the_prose_cites_them opens `pdf = os.path.join(MANUSCRIPTS, "aso", "fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf")` - the journal PDF only. test_the_word_manuscript_is_current_and_whole.py asserts existence, stamp non-collision, source-hash freshness, embedded-vs-linked images, and `measured` floors of words>=500, headings>=4, images>=1. test_the_submission_uploads_are_individual_files.py's content check is parametrized over build_submission_parts.PARTS, which is exactly {'title-page','figure-legends'} - not the manuscript .docx. I verified the .docx IS correct today: 23 entries under numId 1, abstractNum lvl0 `w:start=1` `numFmt=decimal`, in the prose's first-citation order, 22 doi.org hyperlink targets (ref 6 has no DOI upstream either), and the builder's own counts reproduce the stamp exactly (words 5525, headings 19, images 1). The .docx and the PDFs share one HTML pipeline (build_submission_docx.py imports build_submission_pdf.assemble), and this repository has already shipped the defect where an HTML <ol> renumbered from 1 in the built artefact while the markdown was correct.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any change to how the references splice or how LibreOffice numbers the <ol> - a second numbered list earlier in the body sharing numId 1, a converter upgrade, a change to the References anchor - would renumber or drop the .docx reference list with the stamp still matching, the floors still clearing, and the PDF gate still green over a different file. A Qeios reader following superscript 8 would land on the wrong paper.

p1s.summary: The guard that is supposed to warn the publisher when the Zenodo draft is stale is satisfied, at this pin, by the sentence asserting the draft is NOT stale.
p1s.evidence: test_the_deposit_the_papers_cite_is_current.py::test_a_pending_draft_still_matches_the_tree_it_was_built_from takes the non-matching branch here (bb5655ba != eff125805) and then asserts `re.search(r"re-?run the deposit|new_version=false|refresh the draft", section, re.I)` over section 3's slice. I replicated the exact logic on the committed checklist: it matches, and the matching token is `new_version=false` inside "\u2705 **THE DRAFT IS REFRESHED AND CURRENT WITH THE TREE (2026-08-29).** Dispatched `deposit-zenodo.yml` with `new_version=false` at `f6e313d98`" - a past-tense report that the refresh already happened, i.e. the opposite of the instruction the assertion's own failure message demands ('nothing in the preprint checklist tells whoever publishes it to refresh the draft first'). The guard's own comment anticipates a weaker version of this ('the refresh instruction could be demoted to a superseded, retained note further down'); the token surviving inside a completed-status line is one level past what it was hardened against. Log: s20-citations-log.txt.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: It is already satisfied vacuously. Any future refresh followed by any commit that touches a deposited file reproduces the same green: the completed-status sentence keeps the regex satisfied forever, so the gate can never fire again unless someone deletes that sentence. A phrase match cannot distinguish an instruction from a report that the instruction was already carried out; the check needs to key on the recorded digest rather than on prose.

p1s.summary: The archive manifest's promise-to-file mapping checks its quoted promises against the extended report only, so the journal article's own Data availability wording is bound to nothing.
p1s.evidence: aso_archive_manifest.py line 72: `PAPER = os.path.join(ASO, "fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md")`, and the `_promise_still_in_manuscript` flag on every promise row is computed as `_promise_text_found_in_paper(paper, row.get("quote", row["promise"]))` against that one file. The journal article's Declarations says "All code, graded artefacts, per-design tables, every screen's parameters and the complete bounds on each claim are deposited under [DOI]" and "the complete correction record is released with the archive" - wording that appears in no promise row's `quote`. Of the tests that touch the archive, test_the_archive_contains_every_paper_the_builder_builds.py checks only that each citing paper, its built PDFs and their stamps are inside the manifest; test_aso_archive_manifest_vocabulary.py checks junction-label vocabulary and on-disk agreement; test_aso_deposition_doi_is_one_fact.py checks the DOI string. None reads the journal article's promise nouns.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Editing the journal article's Data availability to promise something the archive does not carry - a new artefact class, a supplementary file, a raw-sequence bundle - would leave every gate green, because the only mechanism that asks 'you said X is released, where is it?' re-reads the extended report. The manifest's `gaps.promises_resolving_to_no_file` would stay empty because the new promise never became a row.

p1s.summary: The .docx - the deliverable the gated act consumes - has its sha256 recorded nowhere. Its build stamp pins only its INPUTS, the archive manifest omits every .docx while listing all four PDFs, and the completeness gate reads the builder's self-reported `measured` block rather than the file on disk. An out-of-band edit or re-save of the Word file leaves every gate green.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article-manuscript.docx.build-stamp.json carries `built_from` (four source hashes plus the figure raster) and `measured` = {headings: 19, images: 1, words: 5525}; it carries no digest of the .docx itself. research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_word_manuscript_is_current_and_whole.py: `test_the_word_file_is_not_stale` hashes only the entries of `built_from`; `test_the_conversion_did_not_quietly_drop_the_manuscript` asserts on `_stamp().get("measured", {})`, i.e. the number the builder wrote, not a recount from the archive. Only `test_the_figure_travels_as_bytes_rather_than_as_a_link` opens the .docx at all, and it inspects word/media and the rels, not the text. research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json `files` contains zero entries ending in .docx (I enumerated them) against eight ending in .pdf, so `--check-archive` does not cover it either. I verified the current file is faithful: extracting word/document.xml gives text matching the pinned .md section for section, including the reagent sequences, the eight/nine duplex lengths, both tables and the figure legend.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Anyone opening the .docx in Word or LibreOffice to adjust formatting for the Qeios upload and saving it - the single most likely thing to happen to this file between now and the post - can alter or drop text (a sequence digit, the 'not for administration' declaration, a whole section) and every guard stays green, because the inputs still hash correctly and the stamp still reports 5525 words. The same is true of a truncated or partially-written build whose stamp is left from a prior run. Recording the .docx's own sha256 in the stamp and asserting it, and recounting headings/words from the archive rather than from `measured`, closes it.

p1s.summary: The escape hatch in test_a_pending_draft_still_matches_the_tree_it_was_built_from matches a HISTORICAL mention of the refresh, not an instruction to refresh — so the gate is green today while the checklist tells the publisher the opposite of what the gate believes it was told.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_deposit_the_papers_cite_is_current.py, lines 226-234: when the recorded upload digest differs from the manifest's digest, the test only requires re.search(r"re-?run the deposit|new_version=false|refresh the draft", section, re.I) over the §3 slice of the checklist. Replayed at the pin (log section '=== guard replay ==='): the digests DO differ (bb5655ba9f1a… vs eff1258052fb…) and the regex matches 'new_version=false' — inside the sentence "✅ **THE DRAFT IS REFRESHED AND CURRENT WITH THE TREE (2026-08-29).** Dispatched `deposit-zenodo.yml` with `new_version=false` at `f6e313d98`". That is a record of a refresh that already happened, and the paragraph three lines below it says the only remaining act is to publish. The guard's own docstring names this exact shape ("the refresh instruction could be demoted to a 'superseded, retained' note further down while the blocking item itself said publish as it stands — every phrase still present, the gate still green"); the failure it anticipated is live, because the same words appear in the completed-work line.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: It is already broken in the direction that matters: nothing in the suite can now distinguish 'the checklist tells you to refresh' from 'the checklist tells you it was already refreshed'. Any future refresh whose record stays in §3 keeps the gate green forever, however far the tree walks. The fix is to require the instruction inside the remaining-acts list (or to compare the digest against the acts block), not a substring anywhere in §3.

p1s.summary: The new null-ensembles binding reads only the count, never the clause that says how the ensembles were built, so the construction description can be rewritten to anything and the suite stays green.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py line ~252: _every_site(prose, r"(\w+) null ensembles were built", _word(len(arms)).capitalize(), "how many null ensembles §8 says were built and screened"). The pattern stops at 'were built'; nothing reads 'as scrambles of each design and as chimeras joining the same two parent transcripts at real exon termini'. I confirmed by running the module against the pinned artifacts in a scratch copy: 25 passed, including this test, while that clause is false for four of the ten arms (see blocker 2). The suite also has no assertion tying any prose to aso-parent-null.json's arm NAMES.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any rewording of the construction clause — including one that swaps 'scrambles' for 'random 16-mers' or drops the exon-terminus qualifier — passes silently, because the only bound token is the numeral. A guard that binds the count of a list while leaving the list's description unread is how a correct number ends up certifying a wrong sentence.

p1s.summary: The assumed replicate standard deviation of 0.35 — the single input the manuscript's power figures are computed from — is stated twice, in the manuscript prose and as SIGMA in aso_falsification_power.py, and no instrument in the repository compares the two. Changing either alone leaves every test green and the manuscript internally inconsistent.
p1s.evidence: The article states 'At an assumed replicate standard deviation of 0.35 on the natural-log scale ... six independent biological replicates give about 80% power to falsify a true selectivity of 3 and three give about 30%' (research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md line 319; present verbatim in the .docx). The producing module holds `SIGMA = 0.35` (research/manuscripts/aso_falsification_power.py line 43) and I reproduced its output exactly: n=3 power 30.42%, n=6 81.28%, void_sd 0.648/1.534/2.250 — matching every printed figure. The guard, `test_the_falsification_power_figures_are_derived_not_typed` in research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py, binds the OUTPUTS (power at 6 and 3, TRUE_SELECTIVITY, the three void SDs) but never reads '0.35' out of the prose. The sibling guard `test_the_falsification_cut_is_the_stated_value` in research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_paper_states_what_its_own_claims_depend_on.py line 216 pins the OTHER pre-registered constant, asserting `re.search(r'cut of 5\.0', text)` against the article source — so CUT is guarded in both directions and SIGMA in neither. `git grep '0.35'` across research/manuscripts/tests and research/modalities/tests returns no assertion reading the article's stated SD.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Editing the prose alone to a different assumed SD — e.g. 'a replicate standard deviation of 0.45', a plausible revision after a pilot — leaves SIGMA=0.35 in the module, so the guard still recomputes 81.28%/30.42%, still finds 'about 80%'/'about 30%' in the prose, and passes; the printed power is then wrong for the printed assumption by a wide margin (at sigma=0.45 the true figures are 60.9% and 21.3%; at 0.50, 52.3% and 18.4%). The converse edit is equally silent: changing SIGMA in the module forces the prose power figures to be updated to match, and the prose '0.35' is then stale with nothing reading it. Note that void_sd does not depend on SIGMA, so the 0.65/1.53/2.25 figures would not move and would give no signal either way.
p1s.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md (line 319) and its build product research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article-manuscript.docx — the Qeios deliverable; the unguarded pair is (that prose, research/manuscripts/aso_falsification_power.py SIGMA).
